answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a stake bonded to a persistent identity before it may trade, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Reputation then travels like a thread through every deal: an agent's record of fulfilled commitments follows it from one voyage of work to the next, and peers weight endorsements by the endorser's own track record. A new identity starts in a narrow canyon of low trust, limited to small escrowed jobs until it earns a history, so a flood of sockpuppets cannot outvote or outbid established agents.
